findings.text: Boot-time option parser for the power-management facility consumes a comma-separated string and adjusts global configuration. It recognizes enable and disable requests, timing tunables and boolean toggles with alternate spellings and a negation prefix, then reports success unconditionally.

Option matching tolerates dash and underscore variants and inverts boolean toggles when a negation prefix is present. Entries are separated by commas with surrounding separators skipped, null or empty input ends processing, and one multiprocessor-related toggle also forces a specific idle threshold value.

User-visible control surface consists of a misc device identity plus a file operation table providing open, release, read, poll, ioctl and seek handling, and a proc entry established during initialization. Registration failure of the misc device is logged but does not fail initialization.

Platform quirk handlers keyed by firmware identification each report success and conditionally set a single persistent flag controlling disablement, idle prohibition, interrupt permission, real-mode power-off mode, or power-status interpretation. Handlers emit an informational message naming the matched platform and leave already-set flags unchanged where a guard is present.

Quirk database is a static init-time table pairing firmware match tuples over system, board and BIOS fields with one handler and an identity label, covering multiple vendors and ending with an empty sentinel. Matching relies on external firmware database evaluation before other initialization checks.

Lifecycle moves from firmware quirk evaluation through BIOS presence and capability gating to segment establishment, proc creation, background thread start and optional idle integration, with teardown reversing idle, power-management engagement, device, proc and thread resources. Early refusal leaves the facility disabled, while a multiprocessor power-off-only configuration returns success without exposing full controls.

Initialization enforces capability preconditions including presence of 32-bit support, absence of ACPI override, multiprocessor safety unless explicitly permitted, user enablement, non-zero BIOS version and absence of a specific low-power platform. Version quirks normalize a misreported revision and clear a segment length for older revisions, debug reporting of entry and segment extents is conditional, and background activity plus timing scaling and idle registration occur only after gating passes.

Unsafe configurations are contained by refusing full operation on multiprocessor systems without explicit opt-in, yielding to ACPI, and disabling the facility or its idle calls on machines known to crash or hang. Segment descriptors are programmed only for the pinned processor using a conservative limit, thread start failure cleans up the proc entry, and teardown disengages power management only when previously engaged and above a minimum connection version.

Common offset specification covers boot parameters, processor identification, task stack and protection, hibernation linkage, entry and task-state areas, register save sizing, translation-buffer state, virtualization and confidential-compute state, compatibility signal layouts, cryptographic context and patching metadata, with several groups emitted only when the corresponding build option is active.

32-bit offset specification provides positions for saved instruction, flags, prior stack, general registers and segment selectors within the register save area, plus hibernation descriptor location, a derived distance between entry stack top and task stack pointer held in the task state, and the virtual-address-map operation within runtime service tables.

64-bit offset specification provides control-register plus descriptor positions within saved processor context and general register plus flag positions within the register save area, with additional virtualization steal-time and paravirtual interrupt state emitted only when those configurations are enabled.

Assembly-visible numeric names generated for cross-language layout agreement include families for processor info, task state, signal compatibility, virtualization, boot parameters, register save area, translation state, entry area, task-state stack slots and exception metadata. Consumers in assembly rely on these names remaining stable for the matched structures.

Module initialization entry performs quirk evaluation, capability checks, processor configuration, service publication and background activity startup, returning zero on success or a negative absence indicator when the BIOS is missing, lacks required support, or is administratively disabled.
Module teardown entry releases idle integration, power-management engagement, device and proc publications and background activity, clearing the global power-off hook when this facility installed it.
Offset generation unit is marked for host-side layout emission rather than normal kernel inclusion.
